patch.value: Changelog safety for closed-item writes is gated on the wrong field: the generator buckets by release tag, so the risky population is 337 items and not the 1,475 the closed_at rule protects

The changelog-safety precondition is stated over the field the generator buckets by, and the statement cites the generator invocation that establishes it; A command classifies any candidate item set as changelog-safe or changelog-risky before the write, so a wave does not have to reason about it from prose; The risky population is reported as a number the project can watch, and shrinks as release attribution is backfilled rather than as closed_at is backfilled; A negative control proves a genuinely risky write is refused or flagged: touching a closed item with no release value must be distinguishable from touching one that has it; The operating documentation that currently states the closed_at rule is corrected, so the next wave does not re-derive the wrong premise
The precondition for touching a closed item is stated over the field the changelog generator actually buckets by, and is checkable before the write

This one premise gates every graph enrichment and backfill wave that touches history. While it is stated over the wrong field it forbids 1,770 safe writes and says nothing useful about the 337 risky ones.
Unblocks pm-hnc9w7, pm-lnrk and the terminal-history enrichment waves, and removes pm-wrbe from the critical path of work it does not actually gate.
A closed-item write is classified safe or risky by a command before it happens, denominated in the release field, and the classification is proven against a real changelog regeneration.
Measured directly this session by regenerating the changelog after touching four closed items: the diff was fifteen lines of intra-section reordering and zero bucket movement.

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value:
## The rule as operated

The standing rule is that touching a closed item updates `updated_at`, the changelog buckets by `updated_at`, and therefore any ad hoc closed-item repair silently drags years-old work into the current release notes. pm-hnc9w7's own body states it, and its `why_now` cites it as the reason the cleanup batch has never been scheduled. The refinement in the operating notes narrows it to closed items lacking `closed_at`.

## What the generator actually does

The checked invocation, from `pnpm changelog:pm:check`:

```
pm changelog generate --output CHANGELOG.md --title Changelog --mode replace \
  --all-release-tags --status closed --exclude-tag changelog-exclude \
  --item-url-base https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm
```

`--all-release-tags` buckets by the item's `release` field. `updated_at` orders rows *within* a bucket. So the field that decides which release section an item appears in is `release`, and `closed_at` is not read at all.

## Measured, not reasoned

Four closed items were touched during the graph hygiene batch: pm-7t04 and pm-v7dj (`release: v2026.5.18`), pm-1p2u (`v2026.6.22`), pm-zdec (`v2026.5.1`). All four lack `closed_at`, so the operating rule classifies every one of them as unsafe.

`pnpm changelog:pm:check` failed as expected. Regenerating to a scratch file and diffing against the committed `CHANGELOG.md` produced fifteen lines:

```
1320a1321 > - SDK invoke helpers ... (pm-1p2u)
1328d1328 < - SDK invoke helpers ... (pm-1p2u)
2153a2154,2155 > - Add agent-optimized pm plan command ... (pm-v7dj)
                > - Add pm init checks for AGENTS/CLAUDE ... (pm-7t04)
2161d2162 < - Add agent-optimized pm plan command ... (pm-v7dj)
2165d2165 < - Add pm init checks ... (pm-7t04)
2586a2587 > - Add dependency mutation command ... (pm-zdec)
2593d2593 < - Add dependency mutation command ... (pm-zdec)
```

Every one of the four moved to the top of its own existing release section. No item entered `[Unreleased]`. No section gained or lost an item. The feared effect did not occur, and could not have: the bucket is a function of `release`, which the write did not touch.

## The three populations

Counted across the 2,107 closed item documents:

- 1,770 carry a `release` value. Touching these can only reorder rows inside a section that is already published. Changelog-safe.
- 337 carry no `release` value. These are the only writes whose bucket placement can move. Changelog-risky.
- 1,475 lack `closed_at`. This is the population the operating rule protects.

`closed_at` therefore over-counts the risky set by a factor of 4.4 and, worse, does not contain it: an item can have `closed_at` and no `release`, in which case the rule calls it safe and it is not.

All 98 `no-active-blocker` sentinel holders retired in this session's hygiene batch carry a `release` value. Every one was changelog-safe, and the operating rule had classified all 98 as unsafe because none of them has `closed_at`.

## Consequence for the waves this gates

pm-hnc9w7 is estimated at 900 minutes and blocked partly on this premise. pm-lnrk's Wave 2 terminal-history backfill is scoped as "changelog-safe, epoch-ordered batches" for the same reason. pm-wrbe's deterministic `closed_at` backfill is genuinely valuable for point-in-time reads and history-derived ordering, but it is not the changelog gate it is recorded as being, and holding waves for it is holding them for the wrong reason.

The residual risk is real but small and computable: 337 items, addressable by backfilling release attribution rather than timestamps, and separately owned by the release-attribution work under pm-cpzt82.
